preamble: Final obstruent devoicing turns the voiced retroflex affricate /ɖʐ/ (Polish dż) into voiceless [ʈʂ] utterance-finally. The alternation is visible in native verb forms such as gwiżdżę [ˈɡviʐ.d͡ʐɛ] 'I whistle' beside the imperative gwiżdż [ˈɡviʂt͡ʂ], which is homophonous with Gwiszcz, and in loanwords ending in dż, such as brydż [ˈbrɘt͡ʂ] (genitive brydża) and hadż [ˈxat͡ʂ].

examples.note: Word-final dż is devoiced together with the preceding ż; Wiktionary lists Gwiszcz as a homophone.

examples.from: brydża 'bridge (card game), gen. sg.' (dż before a vowel)
examples.note: Borrowed from English bridge; the final affricate is devoiced.

examples.from: hadż (from Arabic ḥajj, with final dż)

context: Utterance-final position and before voiceless obstruents
